# Registered KERNEL (type-checking) ceilings, milliseconds.
# Generated by scripts/kernel_cost.py --register on the P0 baseline.
# Ceiling = max(measured x 3.0, 50ms): below the floor,
# timing noise dominates and a ratio would fail on a loaded machine.
#
# ⚠️ Tests.Coverage was RAISED from 777 by P1 BATCH 3, deliberately and not by
# --register (which would have loosened every other line at the same time).
# The module went 378ms -> 1960ms, and 1292ms of that is ONE theorem:
# `mem_dest_claims_are_backed`, which reads the table's SHAPES column — prose,
# up to 75 characters a row — as a character list in the kernel.  It is the gate
# that caught a false `m,r (q)` coverage claim that had stood since batch 1 with
# a reassuring comment beside it.  The cheaper design (a Bool field the renderer
# turns into text) was considered and rejected: it makes the prose unable to
# UNDER-claim while leaving it free to OVER-claim, which is the direction that
# actually failed.  A gate on the artifact costs more than a gate on a shadow of
# it, and this is what the difference costs.  See docs/DECISIONS.md D15.
#
# ⭐⭐ P1 BATCH 14 STOPPED RAISING IT AND CHANGED ITS UNITS.  See D38.
# Tests.Coverage's kernel cost is LINEAR IN THE COVERAGE TABLE, which grows
# every batch by construction, so an absolute ceiling on it must be raised every
# batch — and a gate relaxed on schedule is not a gate.  Batch 10 measured 2.4x
# headroom and wrote that there was "room to do this properly rather than under
# pressure"; batches 11-13 did not, and batch 14 arrived at 1.09x.  The ceiling
# is now PER ROW, multiplied by the kernel-pinned `rosterSize`.
#
# ⛔ AND THE ABSOLUTE CEILING PROVABLY MISSED THE REGRESSION THE NEW ONE CATCHES.
# Batch 13 added one theorem costing 12 400ms — measured by batch 14, which also
# found the handed-on figure for it (5 800ms) was low by more than a factor of
# two.  The module went ~90ms/row to 293ms/row, a 3.2x jump in cost per row, and
# the absolute ceiling did NOT fire (17 900 against 19 560).  A per-row ceiling
# at this headroom fires on exactly that.
#
# The registered figure GRANDFATHERS batch 13's theorem rather than pretending
# it is not there: 293ms/row measured x 1.6.  The headroom is tighter than the
# 3.0 used for absolute lines because ordinary GROWTH is now divided out and
# only noise (measured at ~3% across three runs) and real regressions remain.
#
# ⛔⛔ P1 BATCH 20 RAISED IT A THIRD TIME — 470 -> 744 — AND THE HONEST HEADLINE
# IS THAT BOTH REPLACEMENT DESIGNS WERE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT THAT THE
# NUMBER WAS INCONVENIENT.  See D62.
#
# The batch measured 465.1 ms/row against 470: a PASS by 1.05%, which is inside
# this module's own measured load noise.  ⇒ A GATE THAT PASSES BY LESS THAN ITS
# NOISE HAS NOT PASSED; it has produced a reading that would go either way on
# the next machine, and shipping that as green is the phantom this file has
# twice been rewritten to avoid.
#
# The repair batch 17 recorded as blocked WAS unblocked (the block ruled out one
# design, not the goal, and `lean --json` attributes kernel time per
# DECLARATION).  The gate it enabled — no declaration above K x vectorCount —
# was then REFUSED BY ITS OWN SECOND SOURCE: profiled at 700 and at 775 vectors,
# the two declarations holding 53% of this module are barely vector-driven
# (x1.050, x1.077 against an input of x1.107), so a per-vector denominator would
# have gone SLACK exactly where the cost is.  And three declarations grow FASTER
# than their input — `vectorMnemonics` is `eraseDups`, which is QUADRATIC — so
# the "linear in (assertions x vectors)" growth law reported since batch 17 is
# itself wrong, and was only ever inferred from whole-module TOTALS.
#
# ⇒ The number below is now a COARSE TRIPWIRE and no longer pretends to be a
# density law.  The instrument a head should read is the PER-DECLARATION table
# `kernel_cost.py` prints beside it.  The margin is `measured x 1.6`, which is
# the convention this line was REGISTERED with by batch 14 (293 x 1.6 = 470) and
# not a margin invented to fit — the allowance must not come from the thing it
# checks.
#
# ⚠️ THE REAL FIX IS TO MAKE THE MODULE CHEAPER, NOT THE GATE LOOSER, and it is
# named rather than done: `vectorMnemonics`'s quadratic dedup costs ~3.5 s
# across three theorems and grows as the square of a table that grows every
# batch.  Batch 21 should price it.
#
# ⭐ AND Tests.Nonvacuity DELIBERATELY KEEPS AN ABSOLUTE CEILING — it is the
# counterpoint that makes the rule above a rule rather than a habit.  It went
# OVER on the same day (81.5ms against 71) because batch 14 added seventeen
# theorems, four of which draw a 64-bit undefined DESTINATION and so evaluate
# `Oracle.drawVal` sixty-four deep inside a `decide`.  That growth is NOT
# structural: this module grows only when a batch deliberately writes new
# obligations, which is exactly the moment a head should be made to state the
# cost out loud.  A per-row ceiling here would divide out the only signal there
# is.  RAISED to 81.5 x 3.0 = 245 by hand, not by --register.
#
# ⚠️ Measured on an IDLE machine (81.8 / 81.4 across two runs).  The first
# reading was 94ms and was taken while the 21-minute selftest was running; a
# ceiling registered from that number would have been ~15% loose for ever.
X86.Basic 163
X86.Coverage 50
X86.Flags 50
X86.Memory 50
X86.Oracle 50
X86.Semantics 50
X86.Serialize 50
X86.State 50
X86.Syntax 124
X86.Theorems 540
X86.Value 61
X86 50
X86Native 106
Tests.Anchors 801
# ⭐⭐ P1 BATCH 21 — LOWERED 744 -> 493, and lowering is the direction nobody
# polices.  D63 took Tests.Coverage from 37 900 to 22 400 ms by paying each
# group's sweeps once instead of once per theorem, so the ceiling batch 20 set
# at `measured x 1.6` (465.1 -> 744) now stands at 2.4x headroom.  A tripwire
# with 2.4x headroom will not notice a doubling.  Re-registered at the same
# convention batch 14 registered this line with, on the WORST of four readings.
#
# ⚠️ AND THE CONDITIONS, because a figure without them cannot be compared:
# 24 900 / 25 900 / 25 800 / 24 900 ms at one-minute loads of 7.85 / 11.45 /
# 10.58 / 10.76 — a NEIGHBOURING PROCESS was running two `lean` jobs at 100%
# throughout.  The quiet reading taken earlier in this same batch, before
# `cmpxchg8b` added its row, was 22 400 ms at load 3.4.  So this ceiling is set
# from a CONTENDED measurement and is therefore on the LOOSE side of where a
# quiet one would put it: 25 900 / 84 = 308.3 ms/row, x1.6 = 493.3.  That
# direction is the safe one for a tripwire (it cannot fire spuriously) and it is
# stated rather than left for the next head to infer.  A quiet re-measurement
# can tighten it further.
#
# ⚠️ AND THE STANDING OBJECTION IS UNCHANGED: this allowance is derived from a
# measurement of the very thing it checks, so it drifts with its subject and has
# to be re-registered whenever the module moves.  That is a chore, not a gate.
# D62 designed the replacement and its own second source refused it; D63 says
# what a replacement now has to handle.
# ⭐⭐ P1 SEAL (D68) — Tests.Coverage IS NO LONGER GATED PER ROW.
# The helm, 13:37: "a number measured in the wrong unit and applied with care is
# still the wrong number." D62 proved the ROW is not this module's unit; every
# refinement since batch 14 went into the margin and none into the denominator.
# These four ceilings are ABSOLUTE MILLISECONDS and divide by nothing.
#
# Registered at `measured x 1.6` (batch 14's convention for this line) on the
# WORST of four profiles taken after the batch-21 selftest finished, at
# one-minute loads 3.25 / 3.65 / 4.77 / 5.37 — inside the 2.2-4.1 band this
# script MEASURED as having no effect on this module, except the two above it,
# which is why the worst reading is the one used.
#
#     memDestSweep                        11 800 · 12 100 · 11 900 · 11 900
#     pre_states_have_a_returnable_frame   1 800 ·  1 800 ·  1 690 ·  1 820
#     vectorCoverage                       1 440 ·  1 410 ·  1 410 ·  1 450
#
# ⛔ ONLY THESE THREE ARE GATED INDIVIDUALLY, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY: below
# about a second the run-to-run spread reaches 38% (table_mnemonics_subset_roster
# read 708 and then 513) and the COUNT of attributed declarations moved 26/27/28
# between runs. A ceiling there would be noise with a margin on it.
# Everything else is gated as ONE ABSOLUTE TAIL.
Tests.Coverage @decl memDestSweep 19360
Tests.Coverage @decl pre_states_have_a_returnable_frame 2912
Tests.Coverage @decl vectorCoverageXX 2320
Tests.Coverage @tail 12420
Tests.Nonvacuity 245
Tests.Vectors 50
Tests 50
